card.name: Prepositions in 19th-century scientific prose
card.fires_on: Small linking words (by, on, of, such, distinct) inside long, formal, old-style philosophical or natural-history sentences. Seen in Darwin-like essays about species, laws and evidence.

modes.label: Prepositions after verbs
modes.description: A preposition such as by or on following a passive or dependent verb in an argument about laws or facts.
modes.example: cannot be owing to mere changes in marine currents or other causes more or less local and temporary, but depend<< on>> general laws which govern the whole animal kingdom

modes.label: Words before abstract nouns
modes.description: Determiners or adjectives like distinct, such or every just before nouns like evidence, points or one.
modes.example: We have<< distinct>> evidence on this head, in the plants

card.plain: It fires on little linking words in dense, old-fashioned scientific essays that argue about laws and evidence.
